title: SET Instructions
description:
## `movzx`
`movzx` means **move with zero extend**. `setg` only sets `al` (8 bits). The rest of `rax` could be garbage. `movzx rax, al` copies `al` into `rax` and fills the upper 56 bits with zeros. ## SET Instructions
`set` instructions store the result of a comparison as a byte (0 or 1) in a register. They check the flags set by `cmp` or `test`.

```asm
cmp rax, rbx
sete al        ; al = 1 if equal, 0 if not
setne al       ; al = 1 if not equal
setg al        ; al = 1 if greater
setl al        ; al = 1 if less
setge al       ; al = 1 if greater or equal
setle al       ; al = 1 if less or equal
```

Useful for storing boolean results without jumping:
```asm
cmp rdi, 10
setg al         ; al = 1 if rdi > 10
movzx rax, al   ; zero-extend al to full rax
```

`movzx` zero-extends a smaller register into a larger one.


---
## Assignment:
Write a function `is_positive` that takes a number in `rdi` and returns 1 if it's greater than 0, otherwise 0. Use `cmp`, `setg`, and `movzx`. No jumps allowed!
setupCode:
section .data
    pass_msg db "PASS", 10
    pass_len equ $ - pass_msg
    fail_msg db "FAIL", 10
    fail_len equ $ - fail_msg

section .text
    global _start
starterCode:
is_positive:
    ; return 1 if rdi > 0, else 0. No jumps!
    ret
runHarness:
_start:
    mov rdi, 5
    call is_positive
    cmp rax, 1
    jne .fail
    mov rdi, -3
    call is_positive
    cmp rax, 0
    jne .fail
    mov rdi, 0
    call is_positive
    cmp rax, 0
    jne .fail
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, pass_msg
    mov rdx, pass_len
    syscall
    jmp .exit
.fail:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, fail_msg
    mov rdx, fail_len
    syscall
.exit:
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
